summary: Security fix for apps with piiShield (all versions since 0.1.0): a known value inside a longer one left the rest of the longer one in plain text for the model, and a suffixed pseudonym (Anna Müller-1) was restored to the wrong person. Upgrade now.
howTo: No code change. Before: the user writes max@firma.de, a tool result holds johannes.max@firma.de, the model got johannes.<pseudonym>; https://firma.de known made https://firma.de/u/max.mustermann@firma.de <pseudonym>/u/max.mustermann@firma.de. Paths: everything through anonymizeResult (tool results, result handles, server approval subject records, view context values); not the message text (outbound). Back translation (inbound, rehydrateArgs): with more than about 100 people a suffixed pseudonym was restored as another person's original plus -1, so a tool call or the chat-memory summary could carry the wrong person's data. Now known values are replaced longest first in one pass, both ways. Pseudonyms are assigned as before; output is byte-identical unless one known value contains another. Sessions: the mapping lives only in process memory, so the upgrade starts with empty sessions as any restart did; within a process, text broken the old way is restored correctly. Check stored chat-memory summaries of large sessions written before the upgrade: they may name the wrong person. Tests that pinned broken output must expect the longer value's pseudonym. An empty original from a detector is now ignored (before, its pseudonym was inserted between every character). Known limit: of two values that overlap without one containing the other (37/1571/24067 known, then 37/1571/24067Z.huber@kanzlei-x.de), the rest of the shorter one (37/1571/) stays in plain text.
